subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw expose workspace-wide and/or system-wide file browsing through core Gateway/UI, and should that happen via a new scoped API instead of removing the existing agents.files.* allowlist?
rationale: This changes who can read or mutate agent workspace and possibly host files, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only API
options.body: Keep the existing allowlisted files API intact and review a rebased, bounded agents.workspace.* implementation for workspace-root operations only.

options.title: Design System Scope Separately
options.body: Treat host filesystem browsing as a separate maintainer design with stronger auth, auditing, read/write limits, and explicit user consent.

options.title: Reject Broad File Browser
options.body: Keep Mission Control limited to bootstrap files and close the broader workspace/system scope after documenting that boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only API
recommendation.body: Keep the existing allowlisted files API intact and review a rebased, bounded agents.workspace.* implementation for workspace-root operations only.

likelyOwner.reason: They have merged history on the agent files UI/API behavior and are the best routing candidate among the observed related owners for a product/security boundary decision.
